newsitem.title: GERMANY: Pro Sieben prices new shares 72 DM.
newsitem.headline: Pro Sieben prices new shares 72 DM.

text.p: German television broadcaster Pro Sieben AG said on Saturday it had priced its new shares at 72 marks, the top of the pre-announced range.
The issue of preferred shares was 50-times oversubscribed, the broadcaster said on its evening news broadcast. Official trade is due to start on July 7.
A total of 850 million shares were ordered, though only 17.5 million are on offer. 52.5 percent of the issue will be placed with German individual investors.
Pro Sieben chief executive Georg Kofler said, "The high demand makes the issue one of the most successful in German stock-market history."
Company executives said a lottery would be used to fill at least part of the orders, but that the allotment would be complicated partly because of the high demand from outside Germany.
The price range was earlier set at 66 to 72 marks, but the shares have already been changing hands at about 100 marks on the grey market.
The issue is being managed by a banking consortium led by BHF-Bank AG, Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG, and Salomon Brothers.
